scenes.line1: How do you patch Windows servers?
scenes.line2: And roll back if it breaks?
scenes.say: How do you patch Windows servers—and what if an update goes wrong?

scenes.label: WSUS
scenes.sub: WSUS, SCCM, and Intune approve and push updates in rings.
scenes.say: Most companies use WSUS, SCCM, or Intune to approve and push updates in waves called rings.

scenes.label: PatchDay
scenes.sub: Patch Tuesday is the second Tuesday monthly.
scenes.say: Patch Tuesday happens on the second Tuesday of every month. That's when most updates drop.
If a patch causes issues, uninstall it with PowerShell or the wusa tool. Decline it in WSUS so it doesn't come back. Then, check if a reboot is pending in the registry.

scenes.title: Uninstall & Check Reboot
scenes.say: Use Get-HotFix to check if a patch is installed, wusa to uninstall it quietly, and Test-Path to see if a reboot is required.

scenes.question: What's the rollback gotcha?
scenes.right: You must decline it in WSUS or SCCM, or it'll reinstall automatically.
scenes.say: Here's the pitfall: if you only uninstall a bad patch, it may come right back. Always decline it in WSUS or SCCM to block it.
